neet_phy_u04_t08_1.working: In a head-on elastic collision between equal masses, the bodies exchange velocities. So the first body stops and the second moves off with speed u.

neet_phy_u04_t08_2.working: Common velocity = (2×6)/6 = 2 m/s. Initial KE = ½×2×36 = 36 J. Final KE = ½×6×4 = 12 J. Loss = 36 − 12 = 24 J.

neet_phy_u04_t08_3.working: For an oblique elastic collision of equal masses with one at rest, the final velocities are perpendicular. The second ball moves at 60° to the original direction. So v1 = u cos30° = √3u/2 and v2 = u sin30° = u/2.

neet_phy_u04_t08_4.working: A is false: only the KE relative to the centre of mass is lost, and KE remains if total momentum is nonzero. R is a correct description of a perfectly inelastic collision.

neet_phy_u04_t08_5.working: v1 = (1−4)/5 × 10 = −6 m/s, so the ball rebounds at 6 m/s and I is false. v2 = 2×1/5 × 10 = 4 m/s, KE2 = ½×4×16 = 32 J out of 50 J = 64%, so II is true.
